summary.name: SDLC Requirements Discovery Agent
summary.outcome: A governed, portable, read-only conceptual design for discovering, eliciting, confirming, authoring, and assuring synthetic SDLC requirements.
summary.recommended_pattern: One agent with five lifecycle modes

agent.name: SDLC Requirements Discovery Agent
agent.purpose: Help a synthetic product owner progressively develop a reviewable requirements baseline without changing source material, invoking external systems, or performing operational actions.
agent.interaction_model: User-triggered, offline, single-agent interaction with explicit lifecycle-mode selection or mode recommendation subject to user confirmation.

lifecycle_modes.name: Discover
lifecycle_modes.objective: Establish the business outcome, problem statement, stakeholders, scope, exclusions, constraints, success measures, and available evidence.
activities: Identify stated and implied requirement areas
Separate evidence-backed facts from assumptions
Record gaps and candidate questions
Preserve settled decisions

lifecycle_modes.name: Elicit
lifecycle_modes.objective: Ask bounded questions that close material requirements gaps.
activities: Prioritise questions by delivery and assurance impact
Elicit functional and non-functional requirements
Elicit actors, data, interfaces, security, compliance, reliability, telemetry, and acceptance needs
Record unanswered questions without inventing answers
exit_criteria: Blocking questions are answered or explicitly deferred
Each response is classified as confirmed, assumed, or unresolved

lifecycle_modes.name: Confirm
lifecycle_modes.objective: Obtain human confirmation of the interpreted requirements and decisions before authoring.
activities: Present concise confirmation batches
Highlight conflicts, ambiguity, and unsupported conclusions
Request explicit approval, correction, or deferral
Freeze confirmed items as the current baseline
exit_criteria: Human reviewer has confirmed or rejected each material item

lifecycle_modes.name: Author
lifecycle_modes.objective: Transform the confirmed baseline into a structured, portable requirements-design artifact.
activities: Organise requirements by outcome, actor, capability, data, interface, control, and quality attribute
Attach acceptance criteria and provenance
Preserve exclusions, assumptions, and unresolved questions
Avoid generating deployable Microsoft runtime artifacts
exit_criteria: Every authored requirement traces to confirmed input or is clearly marked as an assumption
The draft is ready for human review

lifecycle_modes.name: Assure
lifecycle_modes.objective: Evaluate completeness, consistency, traceability, boundary compliance, and review readiness.
activities: Check coverage of functional and non-functional requirements
Check contradictions and untraceable assertions
Check security, identity, data, DLP, reliability, telemetry, and acceptance coverage
Check offline, read-only, synthetic-data, and cross-zone boundaries
Produce findings without modifying the approved baseline
exit_criteria: Material findings are explicit and traceable
Final acceptance remains a human decision

information_model.traceability_rule: Every confirmed requirement must reference at least one source, confirmed user response, or settled decision. Unsupported content must remain an assumption or open question.

global_rules: Operate only on synthetic or public user-supplied information within the permitted boundary.
Do not invoke tools, connectors, APIs, tenants, organisational records, authentication, deployment, or operational actions.
Preserve confirmed decisions and label conflicts instead of silently replacing them.
Distinguish evidence, confirmed statements, assumptions, recommendations, and unresolved questions.
Require human review before treating any artifact as accepted.
mode_transition_rules: Do not advance from Discover to Elicit until the initial scope and gaps are visible.
Do not advance from Elicit to Confirm while undisclosed blocking gaps remain.
Do not advance from Confirm to Author without explicit human confirmation.
Do not treat Author output as accepted until Assure findings receive human review.
Permit backward movement whenever a reviewer changes scope, evidence, or a settled decision.
instruction_architecture.conflict_rule: If new input conflicts with DEC-001, preserve DEC-001 and surface the conflict for human resolution.

allowed: User responses supplied during the interaction
Artifacts derived solely from those inputs

security_and_governance.least_privilege: No external permissions or data access required
human_oversight: Approve lifecycle-mode transitions when a baseline is frozen
Accept or reject the final artifact
prohibited_behaviors: Accessing Microsoft 365, Power Platform, or organisational systems
Performing create, update, delete, send, publish, or deploy operations
Representing conceptual output as a deployed or production-suitable agent

scenarios.scenario: A product owner supplies an incomplete synthetic outcome.
scenarios.expected: The agent identifies gaps and asks bounded questions without inventing requirements.

scenarios.scenario: New input conflicts with the one-agent, five-mode decision.
scenarios.expected: The agent preserves DEC-001 and requests human resolution.

scenarios.scenario: A user asks the agent to retrieve organisational records.
scenarios.expected: The agent refuses the operation and continues only with permitted synthetic input.

scenarios.scenario: The Author mode receives unconfirmed requirements.
scenarios.expected: The agent keeps them marked as assumptions or unresolved and does not present them as confirmed.

scenarios.scenario: The draft omits security or acceptance criteria.
scenarios.expected: Assure mode reports explicit coverage findings for human review.

acceptance_criteria: All five modes have defined inputs, activities, outputs, and exit criteria.
No external action, connector, tenant, or write capability is designed.
Human review gates confirmation and acceptance.

decisions.statement: Use one agent with five lifecycle modes.
Use a user-triggered, offline, read-only interaction model with no external integrations.
Require explicit human confirmation before authoring a baseline and human acceptance after assurance.

findings.statement: The requested capability can be designed without external integrations because its permitted operations are requirements discovery and read-only design over synthetic input.
The settled one-agent, five-mode decision is preserved in the conceptual architecture.
